title: Grateful Dead Live at Ballroom, U. of Co. on 1969-04-13
lineage: SBD> MR> C> D> CD> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Solid soundboard capture of a high‑energy ’69 show with a soaring Dark Star, epic Morning Dew and an unforgettable Eleven.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers clear, well‑balanced sound for a 1969 ballroom gig (Miller transfer), though a few cuts truncate the end of Lovelight and Dark Star. Musically the concert shines – Jerry’s incendiary runs on Dew, a blistering Dark Star, a soaring Eleven with a Stephen intro, plus strong versions of Lovelight, Schoolgirl and Alligator make it a standout performance.

ai_rating.rationale: Numerous detailed 4‑5 star reviews praise the musical performance while noting only minor recording cuts; the abundance of consistent positive feedback yields a strong rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally solid and clear sound (Miller transfer praised), but several edits cut the end of Lovelight, Dark Star and part of the post‑drum jam, leaving the show slightly incomplete.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A high‑energy, well‑paced set that builds from a strong Lovelight opener through tight jams and climaxes with an epic Dark Star and a soaring Morning Dew, keeping the momentum alive despite a few minor missteps.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry’s scorching runs on Dew, his “southern‑rock” guitar tone on Lovelight, and overall stellar lead work throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Phil is praised for being in a “musical world” during Dark Star, with tight bass interplay that intertwines beautifully with the drums and guitars.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ (keyboard) receives strong mentions, especially during the Eleven and Lovelight jams; his presence adds depth to the keyboard texture.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey’s energetic front‑stage clapping and dynamic drumming are noted, with both drummers weaving tightly into the improvisational sections.
